definition: A method from cooperative game theory adapted to machine learning to fairly attribute a model's prediction to the contribution of each individual input feature.
details: Shapley values (as used in tools like SHAP) provide a theoretically grounded way to explain individual model predictions by quantifying how much each feature contributed relative to a baseline.

explainer.lead: Shapley values come from cooperative game theory and are adapted to machine learning to fairly attribute a model's prediction to each input feature. They matter because they offer a principled way to explain individual predictions.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a team wins a prize; Shapley values work out how much of the win each player deserves, fairly, based on what they added.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use them through tools like SHAP to see how much each feature contributed relative to a baseline. The pitfall is computational cost, since the value requires considering many feature coalitions.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, a feature's Shapley value is its average marginal contribution across all possible orderings of features, computed relative to a baseline. Limits include exponential computation and baseline dependence.

explainer.example: For a single prediction, each feature's Shapley value shows how much it moved the output away from the baseline value.

citation.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
